bad.en: (meant: he hates the piano yet plays it very well)
bad.why: The proverb says skill grows from love of the activity, so it contradicts a case of skill without liking.

r: ほとけのかおもさんどまで
mean: even the most patient person gets angry if wronged again and again
lit: even the Buddha's face, only up to three times: if you stroke it a third time, even he gets angry

use.how: A warning that patience has run out, said by or about someone wronged repeatedly, often as a last warning: 仏の顔も三度までだよ。 Also shortened to 仏の顔も三度.

near.t: 二度あることは三度ある
near.diff: 二度あることは三度ある predicts that a thing will happen a third time; 仏の顔も三度まで warns that another offence will exhaust patience.

cue: Your roommate has twice taken your car without asking and you let it go; now they've done it again, and you tell them this is the last time.

ctx.s: 今[いま]までの遅刻[ちこく]は許[ゆる]してきたけど、{仏[ほとけ]の顔[かお]も三度[さんど]まで}だよ。
ctx.en: I've let your lateness go so far, but my patience has its limits.

ctx.s: 「また約束[やくそく]を破[やぶ]ったの？{仏[ほとけ]の顔[かお]も三度[さんど]まで}だからね。」
ctx.en: "You broke your promise again? Even a saint runs out of patience, you know."

ctx.s: いつも優[やさ]しい部長[ぶちょう]が、同[おな]じミスを繰[く]り返[かえ]す部下[ぶか]をついに叱[しか]った。{仏[ほとけ]の顔[かお]も三度[さんど]まで}だ。
ctx.en: Our ever-gentle manager finally scolded the employee who kept making the same mistake. Even the patient have their limits.

ctx.s: {仏[ほとけ]の顔[かお]も三度[さんど]まで}というが、母[はは]の我慢[がまん]もとうとう限界[げんかい]に達[たっ]した。
ctx.en: They say even the Buddha's patience lasts only three times, and my mother's finally ran out too.

ctx.s: 無断[むだん]キャンセルが続[つづ]いた客[きゃく]に、店主[てんしゅ]は「{仏[ほとけ]の顔[かお]も三度[さんど]まで}です」と予約[よやく]を断[ことわ]った。
ctx.en: To a customer who kept cancelling without notice, the owner said his patience had run out and refused the booking.

ctx.s: 隣[となり]の騒音[そうおん]には何度[なんど]も目[め]をつぶってきたが、{仏[ほとけ]の顔[かお]も三度[さんど]}、今回[こんかい]は苦情[くじょう]を言[い]うことにした。
ctx.en: I'd turned a blind eye to the neighbours' noise many times, but patience has limits, and this time I decided to complain.

bad.s: 彼[かれ]は何[なに]をされても怒[おこ]らない。{仏[ほとけ]の顔[かお]も三度[さんど]まで}のような人[ひと]だ。
bad.en: (meant: he never gets angry, he's as patient as a Buddha)
bad.why: It says that patience runs out, not that someone is endlessly patient. For that, say hotoke no you na hito.

bad.s: 二回[にかい]落[お]ちたけど、{仏[ほとけ]の顔[かお]も三度[さんど]まで}だから次[つぎ]はきっと合格[ごうかく]できる。
bad.en: (meant: I failed twice, so third time lucky, I'll pass)
bad.why: That is sando-me no shoujiki. This proverb is about someone's patience running out after repeated wrongs.

r: ふくすいぼんにかえらず
mean: what is done, or a relationship that is broken, cannot be undone
lit: spilled water does not go back into the basin

story.text: Lü Shang (Taigong Wang) was so poor and so absorbed in study that his wife left him. Later he rose to high office, and she came back asking to be his wife again. He poured a basin of water onto the ground and told her to put it back. When she could not, he told her that a couple once parted cannot come together again, just as spilled water cannot return to the basin.
story.source: 《拾遺記》, the tale of Lü Shang (太公望)

use.how: Said of a word, act or broken relationship that cannot be taken back, as a warning or a sober verdict: 一度言ったことは覆水盆に返らずだ。

near.diff: 後悔先に立たず warns that regret comes too late; 覆水盆に返らず states flatly that what is done, or a broken bond, cannot be restored.

cue: Years after walking out on her husband, a woman asks to come back to him, and he quietly answers that it is far too late.

ctx.s: 一度[いちど]言[い]ってしまった言葉[ことば]は取[と]り消[け]せない。{覆水[ふくすい]盆[ぼん]に返[かえ]らず}だ。
ctx.en: Words once spoken can't be taken back. What's done is done.

ctx.s: 誤[あやま]って送[おく]ったメールはもう取[と]り消[け]せない。{覆水[ふくすい]盆[ぼん]に返[かえ]らず}と諦[あきら]めて、相手[あいて]におわびの連絡[れんらく]をした。
ctx.en: The email I sent by mistake couldn't be recalled. Accepting that what's done is done, I contacted the recipient to apologise.

ctx.en: Lost trust is like spilled water: it cannot easily be won back.

ctx.en: I begged my divorced parents to live together again, but my father just smiled quietly and said what's broken can't be mended.

ctx.en: Once a forest's ecosystem is destroyed, it is truly beyond undoing: it never returns to what it was.
